A Balanced Attack

The backfield runs through one man — their top back absorbs 66% of the carries (league ~59%), a true bell-cow share that makes his rushing volume among the safest floors in the sport when the script cooperates.

The Offensive Blueprint

It's a short, rhythm-based passing game — aDOT just 6.9 — that lives on YAC and checkdowns, boosting reception totals over big-play yardage.

By the numbers it's a struggling unit — a 42% success rate (below the 44% average).

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they stay aggressive, throwing 61% of the time, which puts scoring equity on the WR1.

Defense — The Run Comes Free

They surrender 132 rushing and 219 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). The run moves against them — target opposing RB1s.

They leak RB rushing TDs (0.62/game vs ~0.46) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They lock down opposing tight ends — just 30 rec yds/game (vs ~35); fade receiving props there.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: opposing RB1s smash on the ground and at the goal line.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
